findings_addressed: TC-68 — `Engine::open` no longer re-embeds the 45-probe vector-equivalence set on every open. The 0.8.18 verdict is cached against an embedder fingerprint stored in `_fathomdb_open_state`; an open whose fingerprint is unchanged performs ZERO probe embeds.

MEASURE-FIRST (steward seq-111 ordering) — the actual per-open cost was instrumented and recorded BEFORE the fix was written, and the plan's DoD framing was corrected against it rather than built to literally.

The plan's DoD sentence ('open cost independent of enrolled-kind count') was confirmed ALREADY TRUE at baseline, vacuously — the probe gate is `SELECT EXISTS(...)`, not a count, and the body never iterates kinds. A kind-count test would have been a vacuous green; it is instead pinned as an explicit characterization test that says so out loud.

The ruled residual (same-identity backend drift no longer caught per-open) is made explicit and reviewable in a design note, the CHANGELOG, all three interface docs, AND as an executable test assertion.

blockers_encountered.description: 12 of 23 tests in the shipped `vector_equivalence_probe.rs` went RED after the fix. Cause was the residual, not a defect: `seed_references` / `seed_bge_references_with_pinned_mean` leave a CACHED passing verdict, so a subsequent reopen with a divergent/panicking/erroring same-identity backend hits the cache and is never asked to embed.
blockers_encountered.resolution: Added a documented `force_probe_verdict_rerun(path)` helper to that file which drops the `_fathomdb_open_state` marker, and called it at the end of both seed helpers plus two explicit sites (`post_open_registration_...` session 3, `upgrade_from_v18_...` before the divergent open). This puts each workspace in exactly the state a real fingerprint change produces, so the R-VEQ-2/3/4 assertions stay LIVE rather than going vacuous. Deliberately NOT done by relaxing any assertion. All 23 pass.

blockers_encountered.description: The `EmbedderIdentity` triple can never be observed to change at the probe — `check_embedder_profile` refuses the open with `EmbedderIdentityMismatch`/`EmbedderDimensionMismatch` first — so the plan's 'with the probe still running on an identity change' cannot be exercised end-to-end via identity.
blockers_encountered.resolution: Not a blocker for the requirement (it is satisfied a fortiori: an identity change never reaches a cached verdict). The identity triple is still IN the fingerprint as defence-in-depth, and the two fingerprint axes that ARE reachable end-to-end — the pinned `mean_vec` and the stored baseline blobs — are each covered by a test. Documented in design note §2.1.

additional_changes_made_in_scope: The cache gate is placed AFTER the 0.8.18 fix-2 stored-baseline completeness validation, not before it. Everything cheap (row count, contiguous ordinals, probe_text vs fixture, blob length, stored identity) still runs on EVERY open and still fails closed; only the 45 model invocations are skipped.

The fingerprint hashes the stored `reference_vec` BLOBS, not just row shape. fix-2 pins each row's shape but not its blob CONTENT — that was caught implicitly by the re-embed diverging. Without this input, caching the re-embed away would silently re-open the fix-2 external-tamper fail-open. Cost is ~69 KB of SHA-256 against 45 model calls.

Every `Err` path of the check now CLEARS the cached marker (wrapper `probe_check_against_baseline` around a new `probe_check_against_baseline_inner`), so an unverifiable workspace never leaves a stale 'verified' marker for a later open to match.
`type StoredProbeRow` alias introduced for the 6-tuple baseline row (also keeps clippy::type_complexity off the new fn signature).

Three characterization tests that PASS at baseline and must stay green were added alongside the RED ones, pinning the measured 0 / 90 / 45 figures and the kind-count flatness so the numbers in the design note are executable, not prose.

ONE enrolled kind = 90 / 45 / 45 across opens 1-3. SIX enrolled kinds = 90 / 45 / 45 — IDENTICAL. So 45 AND 90 are BOTH true, of different opens: 90 is the ONE-TIME population open (45 in `probe_populate_baseline` to persist the references + 45 more because `probe_populate_or_check` immediately runs the fix-2 'confirm the just-written baseline' check), and 45 is EVERY open thereafter, forever. The ledger's '90 synchronous embeds' and the fixture's 45 were being quoted about different opens; neither was wrong. The population open is deliberately LEFT at 90 (shrinking it would trade the fix-2 guard for a one-off saving). || FINGERPRINT INPUTS, exactly: SHA-256 over length-prefixed fields — (1) recipe tag `fathomdb-veq-verdict-v1`; (2) identity.name / .revision / .dimension [defence-in-depth ONLY — `check_embedder_profile` refuses the open first, so unreachable here]; (3) whether mean-centering applies + the live pinned `mean_vec` bytes [LOAD-BEARING: P1 quantizes sign(x - mean_vec), and open-time mean-recovery/requantize and the operator `recompute_mean` verb both rewrite it, so an identity-triple-only key would be stale by construction]; (4) `VECTOR_EQUIVALENCE_PROBE_FIXTURE`; (5) `VECTOR_EQUIVALENCE_P1_FLIP_FLOOR` and `VECTOR_EQUIVALENCE_L2_EPSILON`; (6) the stored baseline rows INCLUDING the reference blobs. On the fixture-digest question you asked me to decide: the drift test does NOT make it redundant (it pins the engine copy equal to the embedder-crate copy — COPY drift between two committed files, not content across releases). The fix-2 completeness check does independently fail CLOSED first on a fixture edit, so the digest is belt-and-braces; I kept it anyway because it costs one hash of a ~3 KB constant and makes the fingerprint a self-contained statement of what the verdict depended on rather than relying on a second mechanism failing closed first. Reasoning in design note §2.3. || STORAGE: one row in `_fathomdb_open_state(key,value)` — migration step 1, the engine's existing open-time durable-marker KV table alongside `projection_cursor`, `search_index_tokenizer_reproject_complete`, `tc33_edge_vector_prune_complete`, `tc33_reserved_write_cursor`. Key = `vector_equivalence_verified_fingerprint`. So NO `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump, NO migration step, and not even the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`-at-open route you suggested — the table already exists on every migrated DB. No schema-drift assertion is affected: the schema crate's step tests assert per-step DDL and index shape, none enumerates `_fathomdb_open_state` ROWS; `cargo test -p fathomdb-schema` green. || THE RESIDUAL, one sentence: a backend that drifts WITHOUT changing its declared identity (candle CPU<->CUDA, a rebuilt library/driver) moves no fingerprint input, so the cached verdict answers and the drift is no longer caught on any open — it is caught only at the next open whose fingerprint does change, which by definition a pure backend swap is not. || SDK TEST FILES TOUCHED: NONE, in any language — and this is a deliberate, reasoned decision I am flagging loudly rather than an omission. TC-68 adds no public surface (no type, field, method or error), the X1 probe suites (`src/python/tests/test_vector_equivalence_probe.py`, `src/ts/tests/vector-equivalence-probe.test.ts`) are surface-parity-only by their own docstrings and explicitly defer divergence behaviour to the Rust engine suite, AND the probe is unreachable from a default SDK session (no live embedder without `use_default_embedder` / `useDefaultEmbedder`, which needs weights/network). Any mirror I wrote would have been green without exercising the cache — the exact vacuous-green trap you warned about. I documented the one consumer-observable semantic shift in `dev/interfaces/{rust,python,typescript}.md` and CHANGELOG.md instead. If you want the live harness run anyway, there is nothing new to run; if you disagree with the call, the honest non-vacuous SDK test would require an SDK session with a real embedder, which no existing SDK test has. || FOR YOUR SIGN-OFF QUEUE (§3.5 — described, NOT implemented): the ONE change that would genuinely retire the residual is widening `EmbedderIdentity` (or the `Embedder` trait) with a RUNTIME BACKEND/DEVICE DESCRIPTOR — e.g. `candle-cuda:driver=12.4`, or a build/feature fingerprint — and folding it into the verdict fingerprint. `EmbedderIdentity` is `{name, revision, dimension}` today with no such field and the trait reports nothing else, so this is public-surface work on a governed type and needs HITL sign-off. It belongs with the batched governed-surface decision the plan places AFTER Slice 22. Recorded in design note §6.2; NOT taken here. || OTHER DEVIATIONS, stated loudly: (1) I modified the shipped `vector_equivalence_probe.rs` — 44 lines, adding a documented `force_probe_verdict_rerun` helper and 4 call sites. Without it 12 of its 23 tests would have gone VACUOUS (asserting a divergence is caught on an open where the probe never ran). No assertion was relaxed. This is the one place a reviewer should look hardest. (2) I split `probe_check_against_baseline` into a thin wrapper + `_inner` so every failure path clears the cache; the wrapper is the only new control flow in the shipped path. || SUGGESTED REVIEWER FOCUS for codex §9: (a) is the cache gate's placement after the fix-2 completeness validation genuinely sufficient to preserve the external-tamper closure, given the blob digest is in the fingerprint; (b) is swallowing a cache-WRITE failure right (I argue yes — the arm was just verified, and the consequence is the next open re-runs, i.e. more work not less); (c) does `force_probe_verdict_rerun` in the shipped suite hide anything a reviewer would want asserted differently.
